segments.he: מַכִּירִים אַתֶּם אוֹתוֹ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַכִּירִים אַתֶּם אוֹתוֹ? נׇכְרִי הָרַג? יִשְׂרָאֵל הָרַג? הִתְרִיתֶם בּוֹ? קִיבֵּל עָלָיו הַתְרָאָה? הִתִּיר עַצְמוֹ לְמִיתָה? הֵמִית בְּתוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that after the interrogations the court asks several questions essential to the testimony, such as: «Do you recognize him? The Sages taught» in a baraita: In a trial for murder, the court asks the witness: «Do you recognize» the accused? «Did he kill a gentile? Did he kill a Jew? Did you forewarn him? Did he accept the forewarning on himself,» i.e., acknowledge the warning? «Did he release himself to death,» i.e., acknowledge that he is aware that the court imposes capital punishment for murder? «Did he kill within» the time required «for speaking» a short phrase, as if not, he could claim he forgot the warning?
